questions.question: Why should you do the same pre-trip inspection steps in the same order each time?

options.text: You will be less likely to forget a step.
The form must be followed in order.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will be less likely to forget a step.
questions.explanation: Doing an inspection the same way each time helps you learn the steps. Having a routine makes it less likely you will skip something.

questions.question: The easiest way to notice that your trailer is skidding is to:

options.text: Use your mirrors to check if the trailer has left the lane.
Release the brake pedal and then push it down again.
Watch the jackknife warning light on the control panel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your mirrors to check if the trailer has left the lane.
questions.explanation: Use your mirrors to spot a trailer skid. When you brake hard, check your mirrors to make sure your trailer is still in the right position.

questions.question: If you feel tired while driving, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Get some rest.
questions.explanation: If you feel tired while driving, stop and get sleep. This is the only safe choice. Fighting fatigue and continuing to drive is very dangerous and can cause a deadly crash. Pills may keep you awake, but they will not make you more alert.

questions.question: Having anti-lock brakes on only one axle:

options.text: Will not make a difference in braking.
Will give you better control when braking.
Will likely cause the air brakes to break.

questions.correctAnswerText: Will give you better control when braking.
questions.explanation: If a vehicle has anti-lock brakes on one axle, the driver will have more braking control than without any anti-lock brakes.

questions.question: Looking far ahead of your vehicle while driving is:

options.text: Not helpful, because you cannot act on things far ahead.
Good practice to spot hazards early.
Only required if you are carrying hazardous materials.

questions.correctAnswerText: Good practice to spot hazards early.
questions.explanation: Good drivers look 12 to 15 seconds ahead. This gives you time to spot hazards early and respond safely.

questions.question: A manifest for transporting hazardous waste:

options.text: Must be attached to the outside of the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must be signed by hand.
questions.explanation: When carrying hazardous waste, you must have a Uniform Hazardous Waste Manifest with you. It must be signed by hand.

questions.question: In a pre-trip inspection, you should check for all of the following, except:

options.text: Tires with too much air pressure.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tires made by different manufacturers.
questions.explanation: Check that your tires have enough tread depth. Front tires need at least 4/32 of an inch; other tires need at least 2/32 of an inch. Make sure tires are not worn, cracked, or over or under inflated. All tires should be the same size.

questions.question: If your vehicle is hydroplaning, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Not use the brakes.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle starts to hydroplane, do not brake. Instead, let off the accelerator and push in the clutch. This helps you regain traction.

questions.question: An open car window in cold weather may mean the driver is:

options.text: Using the heat in their vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving impaired.
questions.explanation: Watch other drivers for signs of impaired driving. Drivers who are drunk, tired, on drugs, or sick are hazards. A driver with their window open in cold weather may be impaired.

questions.question: You should always be able to stop within:

options.text: The distance you can see ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The distance you can see ahead.
questions.explanation: Your vehicle must be able to stop within the area of road you can see. Slow down whenever you cannot see far enough ahead.

questions.question: A stopped bus is:

options.text: Not a concern because it is stopped.
A concern only if passengers are getting off.
Always a concern, whether or not you see passengers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always a concern, whether or not you see passengers.
questions.explanation: Always be careful around stopped buses. Passengers may be near the bus. The bus may block your view of passengers, or passengers may not see you.

questions.question: An empty combination vehicle will have:
questions.correctAnswerText: Low traction.
questions.explanation: An empty trailer has less weight. With less weight, the stiff suspension springs and strong brakes will have lower traction. This means the vehicle will take longer to stop than a fully loaded vehicle.

questions.question: Rollovers happen when:
questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers turn too fast.
questions.explanation: Rollovers happen when drivers change lanes or turn too quickly.

questions.question: When checking the engine, you should not:

options.text: Check the windshield washer fluid level.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drain the brake fluid.
questions.explanation: When checking the engine, you should check the oil level, coolant level, and windshield washer fluid level. You should not drain brake fluid.

questions.question: What is reaction distance?

options.text: The distance you travel from when you decide to brake until you actually hit the brakes.
The distance you travel from when a hazard appears until you see it.
The distance you travel from when you see a hazard until you decide to brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: The distance you travel from when you decide to brake until you actually hit the brakes.
questions.explanation: Stopping distance is made up of three parts: perception distance, reaction distance, and braking distance. Reaction distance is how far you travel from the moment you decide to brake until your foot actually hits the brake pedal.

questions.question: If you are unsure whether your vehicle fits under a bridge, you should:

options.text: Swerve while passing under the bridge.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: If you are not sure your vehicle fits under a bridge, slow down. Find another route if possible.

questions.question: Which is not a good rule for using turn signals?

options.text: Do not signal if you think others know what you will do.
Cancel your signal after you finish turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not signal if you think others know what you will do.
questions.explanation: Always use your turn signal when you plan to turn or change lanes. Signal well in advance, keep the signal on during the turn, and turn it off when finished. Never assume others know your plans.

questions.question: To prevent drowsiness while driving, you should:

options.text: Get a good night's sleep before your trip.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get a good night's sleep before your trip.
questions.explanation: Drowsy driving is dangerous. Get full sleep before a trip. Other helpful steps include having a passenger, driving at times when you are normally awake, and avoiding medications that cause drowsiness. Regular exercise also helps you stay alert.

questions.question: After changing a tire, you should stop after a short distance to:

options.text: Check that the wheel nuts are tight.
Check that the tire has enough air.
Verify the correct tire was changed.
Make sure another tire was not damaged.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check that the wheel nuts are tight.
questions.explanation: After changing a tire, stop soon afterward to re-check that the wheel nuts are tight.

questions.question: During a truck fire, before opening trailer doors you should:

options.text: Feel the doors to see if they are hot.
Find someone else to open them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Feel the doors to see if they are hot.
questions.explanation: During a truck fire, check if the trailer doors are hot before opening them. Hot doors mean there may be a cargo fire inside. Do not open the doors because it will bring in oxygen and make the fire worse.
